name: Semantic Headings
description: Checks the H1-H6 outline: at least one heading, exactly one H1, no skipped levels, and not too many generic or very short headings. AI engines use the heading hierarchy to segment content into answerable sections.
inputs: rendered DOM: all h1-h6 elements in document order and their textContent

scoring.summary: No headings at all => 0. Otherwise start at 8: no H1 -3, or more than one H1 -2; -1 per skipped level (a heading whose level > previous heading level + 1; the first heading is never a skip), capped at -2; -1 if more than 3 generic/short headings. Integer score; status from the shared rule (>= 7 pass, >= 4 warning).

rules.condition: document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6').length === 0
skipped level: iterating headings in document order, with lastLevel = previous heading level (starts 0, first heading never flagged), level > lastLevel + 1. Going up (H4 -> H2) is fine.

generic heading: textContent.toLowerCase().trim() length < 3, OR exactly equals one of ['introduction', 'overview', 'welcome', 'about', 'more', 'info', 'content', 'section', 'chapter', 'home']. If count of generic headings > 3

scoring.status_mapping: From the integer score with the shared 80% / 50% rule: 7-8 pass, 4-6 warning, 0-3 fail. Worst case 8-3-2-1 = 2 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Compose the full rendered markup per page in document order: layout header, page body, components, footer. Static HTML: each *.html. Astro: layout + src/pages/** + components (headings in components count). Hugo: baseof.html + single/list templates + partials, plus headings from Markdown content (#, ##, ... map to h1-h6; note Hugo/most themes render the page title as <h1> in the template, so a '# ' in content makes a second H1). Eleventy: layouts + Markdown/Nunjucks content. Next.js: layout.tsx + page.tsx JSX headings, MDX content. Vite SPA: root components and routed views. Extract heading level and text, then apply the rules.

parity.note: The extension counts every h1-h6 in the live DOM, including visually hidden ones, headings in cookie banners, chat widgets, modals and client-rendered content. Source analysis must resolve component composition order and Markdown-to-HTML heading mapping; headings rendered from CMS data or conditionally are uncertain. Text from template variables affects the generic-heading rule.

fix_summary: Ensure exactly one <h1> per page (usually the page title in the layout; demote extra H1s in content or header logos to h2/p), fix skipped levels by changing heading tags in templates/Markdown, and rename generic headings to descriptive text. Tag-level changes can be auto-applied; renaming generic headings needs user content.

divergences.extension: Status: >= 6 pass, >= 4 warning (so 6/8 is a pass).
divergences.plugin: Status from the shared rule: >= 80% (7/8) pass, >= 50% (4/8) warning.
divergences.reason: All checks share one status rule in the plugin.

divergences.extension: Counts every h1-h6 in the live DOM, including headings injected by scripts and widgets.
divergences.plugin: Counts h1-h6 in each built/static HTML file.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: the plugin reads the repo, not a rendered page.
